exposure: Type of infant feeding (breastfeeding vs. artificial milk)
outcome: Maternal quality of life (measured using the SF-36)
Emergency hospital service use for infant health concerns
cohort: 364 healthy primigravida women aged 18-45 years who gave birth to healthy newborns at a public hospital in Madrid, Spain, between February and October 2013
finding: While there was no significant difference in quality of life between breastfeeding and artificial milk feeding groups at six months postpartum, at six weeks postpartum, mothers in the breastfeeding group were more likely to report that their children ate and slept well and did not require emergency hospital visits, which was associated with greater maternal quality of life.
